subject: Sleepefficiency Part 4 compared to EEG data / Sleeponset

messages.author: b418fa99bb00f5cd
messages.subject: Sleepefficiency Part 4 compared to EEG data / Sleeponset
parts:
Dear Vincent,

we ran into an issue with the part 4 sleep cleaned sleepefficiency output when compared to our eeg results. 



we can't explain these differences so far.

in the excel we put the eeg result, the ggir t5A5, the ggir t2.5A5 and our results from our script. 

The correlation of ggir's sleepefficiency with the eeg's sleepefficiency is very low for both of the ggir settings.


The second thing we were having discussions about was  the visual report. 

if the report has the the Filename: NA and also if its named like on the screenshot, it shows the wrong sleeponset time altough we used sleepwindowtype = Time in Bed and it also visually looks like that the onset happened before midnight.

we were also concerned about the colours indicating spt sleep and spt wake. The spt window apparently switches on and off during the day.

We thought that there could be a problem because we are measuring only one night hence the watch would not be able to calibrate itself?



Thank you for your help

Kind regards Markus

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleepefficiency Part 4 compared to EEG data / Sleeponset
parts:
Dear Markus,

I would start by comparing the sleep window start- and end times (onset/wakeup), if they are different then that could be a clue to why sleep efficiency is different. If possible try to make sure that GGIR and EEG analysis use the same bedtime information in the form a sleeplog to guide the GGIR estimates of sleep.

Also note that the definition of 'sleep efficiency' may not be compatible across methods. So far, I have encountered two different definitions of sleep efficiency in the sleep research field:
  1. total time in sleep stage divided by total duration of time inbed
  1. total time in sleep stage divided by total duration of sleep period time window

GGIR uses defintion 1 in GGIRpart4 if sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed", and uses definition 2 in GGIR part5.

Kind regards,
Vincent

parts:
Dear Vincent

Thank you very much for your support.


We used the same bed times for both, the EEG and the actigraphy analysis. Also for the sleep efficiency we used the same definition (definition 1 as in GGIR part 4).


Do you have any suspicion concerning the differences in the visual reports?

- Wrong sleeponsets

(- constantly changing spt window from blue to grey during the day)

For example subject 5202 had a sleeplatency of five minutes (EEG)

This gives us a sleep efficiency of 77.241% GGIR and 96.95% EEG....



Visual Report : after midnight


with kind regards

Markus

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleepefficiency Part 4 compared to EEG data / Sleeponset
parts:
Dear Markus,

The sleep during daytime indicates that something goes wrong with the plot generation itself. We never tailored or tested these plots for use in combination with time in bed diaries. Note that the code to generate the visualisation has always been low on my priority list because most researchers I have worked with were only interested in the quantitative output of GGIR (csv reports). The visualisations have not been part of the evaluation and may therefore still come with some mistakes.

Another source of the problem could be that you are trying to detect sleep from less than a day worth of data. GGIR has been designed to process multi-day data. To use it in a sleep clinic setting you may need to append simulated data before and after the recording, like I did in https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30154500/. Another option is not to rely on GGIR for onset and wake-detection, but use the polysomnography estimates of onset/wake, and only rely on GGIR for the sleep/wake patterns within that window. Either way, this is a non-typical use-case of GGIR.

To move forward, you could either investigate it yourself and try to address the underlying issue (all GGIR code is on GitHub and I welcome outside contributions). Alternatively, I would be happy to work on this as a paid consultancy. If you are interested then send me a personal message such that we can discuss details.

With kind regards,

Vincent

Dear Vincent,

Is it possible (and by which software?) to merge two bin files, i.e. the seven days and the subsequent eeg night?
This would theoretically circumvent our multi-day-data problem by allowing us to subsequently set nrnights to 8 and have the missing time for the tasks in the lab displayed as no wear time.
Am I right with this consideration?

kind regards

Markus
